title: Add logging support for better observability
body:
## Feature Request

### Summary
The project would benefit from structured logging to make it easier to debug issues in production.

### Motivation
Currently it can be difficult to understand what the application is doing at runtime without adding print statements. Proper logging would:

- Allow users to control verbosity with log levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR)
- Make it easier to integrate with log aggregation systems
- Help diagnose issues in production without code changes

### Proposed Implementation
```python
import logging

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def my_function():
    log.debug("Starting my_function")
    # ... 
    log.info("my_function completed successfully")
```

### Impact
Low risk change with high value for users running this in production environments.

comments.body:
This is a generic feature request asking Streamlit to adopt structured logging with Python's `logging` module and configurable log levels. However, Streamlit **already provides this**: `lib/streamlit/logger.py` exposes a `get_logger(__name__)` helper that returns a standard `logging.Logger`, and `set_log_level` supports `CRITICAL`/`ERROR`/`WARNING`/`INFO`/`DEBUG`. The log level can also be configured via the `logger.level` config option (`config.toml`, env var, or CLI flag), and the project's own contributor guide instructs internal code to use this logger. The issue body is high-level and AI-generated (note the `ai-review` label and lack of a concrete gap), so it likely duplicates existing functionality. Several open issues already track real, concrete gaps in Streamlit's logging (suppressing specific messages, writing logs to a file, conforming to Python logging standards, etc.) and are better venues for the underlying concern.

### Related Issues

- [#4742 — Logging strategy should follow the standard](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4742): Long-standing request to make Streamlit's logging configuration play nicely with the standard Python `logging` ecosystem (custom loggers, propagation, etc.) — the most direct overlap with this request.
- [#4539 — Save logs to a text file, as a parameter in the config.toml](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4539): Concrete observability/log-aggregation gap (file sink configurable via `config.toml`) that this generic request would also benefit from.
- [#11645 — Add the ability to mute/disable messages logged by the Logger](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11645): Related request to give users finer-grained control over Streamlit's log output, which is part of "controlling verbosity".
